faqs.q: Sec. 58-1. - Jurisdiction and powers of the municipal court.
faqs.a:
(a)
Creation and governance.
The municipal court, having been established, is governed by the provisions of C.R.S.
               tit. 13, art. 10, as amended, except as otherwise specifically provided in the City
               Charter or in this Code.
(b)
Jurisdiction.
The municipal court has original jurisdiction of all cases arising under the ordinances
               of the city with full power to punish violators thereof by the imposition of such
               fines and penalties as set forth in this Code or by court rule, and by enforcing all
               orders of the court.
(c)
Powers.
The municipal court has all powers relating to the operation of the court as set
               forth in C.R.S. section 13-10-114, as may be from time to time amended, subject to
               any rules of procedure governing the operation and conduct of a court promulgated
               by the Colorado Supreme Court. A municipal court judge has the authority to assess
               fees and costs in accordance with
section 58-13
of this Code and otherwise in accordance with the court's published fines, fees,
               and costs schedule. A municipal court judge may hold a person in contempt as set forth
               herein, and has the power to punish a person deemed to be in contempt.
(1)
Emergency powers.
Upon the declaration by the city manager of a civil emergency, emergency, or local
               disaster under
chapter 26
of this Code, the presiding municipal court judge may issue special, standing, or
               other orders pertaining to court procedures, the location of judicial proceedings,
               and the time frames within which judicial proceedings are held. An order issued under
               this subsection must state the reason or reason the order is necessary, and must comport
               with the Constitutions of the United States and of Colorado.
(i)
An order issued under this subsection may remain in effect for no longer than 91 days,
               unless the emergency declaration that necessitated the order, or an extension thereof,
               is still in effect at the end of the 91 day period. If the emergency declaration or
               extension thereof is still in effect at the end of 91-day period, the presiding judge
               may extend the order another 91 days. An order issued under this subsection shall
               remain in effect even if the emergency declaration under which it was issued, or an
               extension thereof, has been lifted or rescinded, except that it may be lifted or vacated
               at any time by the presiding municipal court judge.
(d)
Procedures.
The procedures of the court shall be in accordance with the Municipal Court Rules
               of Procedure as promulgated by the Colorado Supreme Court. The presiding municipal
               court judge has the authority to issue local rules of procedure consistent with any
               rule of procedure adopted by the Colorado Supreme Court.
(1)
Court of record.
The municipal court shall be a court of record. The presiding municipal court judge
               shall provide for the keeping of a verbatim record of the proceedings and evidence
               at trials by any electronic or other means.
(e)
Sessions of court.
There shall be regular sessions of court for all proceedings held in the municipal
               court, except that a municipal court judge may hold a special session of court at
               any time.
(1)
Sessions open.
All sessions of the municipal court shall be open, except where the nature of the
               case is such that it would be in the interest of justice to exclude persons not directly
               connected with the proceeding. In those cases, a municipal court judge may order that
               the courtroom be cleared of all persons not directly connected with the proceeding.
               A municipal judge may order the general public to be excluded from any hearing, trial,
               or other proceeding involving a juvenile charged with any violation of the Arvada
               City Code other than those set forth in
chapter 54
, motor vehicles and traffic, on its own motion or on the motion of the defense or
               the prosecution if the court determines that it is in the best interest of the juvenile
               or the community to exclude the general public. If such a finding is made, the court
               shall admit only such persons as have an interest in the case or work of the court,
               including persons whom the city attorney, the juvenile, or the juvenile's parents
               or guardian wishes to be present. Notwithstanding the above, the judge retains the
               authority to sequester named or potential witnesses in any proceeding.
(i)
In a case where a person refuses or fails to leave the courtroom after having been
               ordered under this subsection by a municipal court judge to do so, the judge shall
               have the power to order the person to immediately show cause why the person should
               not be punished for contempt for the failure or refusal. If the judge finds that the
               failure or refusal was not justified by good cause or excusable neglect, the judge
               may impose punitive sanctions under its contempt powers under subsection (m) of this
               section.
(f)
Failure to appear for court - defendants.
In a case where a person is summoned to appear, ordered to appear by a municipal
               judge, or ordered to appear as a condition of a bond at the municipal court, and such
               person fails to appear at the time and place designated in the summons or order, the
               judge shall have the power to issue a show cause order for the failure to appear.
               The order shall command the defendant to appear before the municipal court to show
               cause why the defendant should not be punished for contempt. Upon appearance of the
               defendant on such show cause order, if the judge finds that the failure to appear
               was not justified by good cause or excusable neglect, the judge may impose punitive
               sanctions under its contempt powers under subsection (m) of this section.
(1)
Warrants allowed.
Nothing in this section shall prohibit the court from issuing a warrant for a defendant
               who fails to appear.
(2)
Traffic infraction cases.
The municipal court shall not issue a warrant for a defendant's failure to appear
               as ordered in the summons and complaint in a traffic infraction matter. Instead, the
               court is authorized to enter a default judgment in the matter.
(g)
Attendance of witnesses; compliance with process required.
In a case where a person is summoned or subpoenaed as a juror or as a witness to
               the municipal court in accordance with applicable rules of the court and this Code,
               and fails to appear at the time and place designated in the summons or subpoena, the
               judge shall have power to issue a contempt citation to the juror or witness for the
               failure to appear. The citation shall command the juror or witness to appear before
               the municipal court to show cause why that juror or witness should not be punished
               for contempt. Upon appearance of the juror or witness on such show cause order, if
               the court finds that the failure to appear was not justified by good cause or excusable
               neglect, the court may impose punitive sanctions under its contempt powers under subsection
               (m) of this section.
(h)
Attendance of parent in a juvenile matter - required.
In a case where a summons and complaint for a violation of the Arvada City Code is
               issued to a person under the age of 18 years, the municipal court may, when the court
               determines that it is in the best interests of the juvenile to do so, join the juvenile's
               parent as a respondent to the case.
(1)
Joinder process.
The court may advise a parent of being joined as a respondent in a juvenile case
               by issuing a subpoena by certified mail, return receipt requested, addressed to the
               juvenile's address shown on the summons and complaint. The subpoena shall contain
               a copy of the summons and complaint, and an order that the parent appear with the
               juvenile at each court appearance scheduled thereafter. Service by mail is complete
               upon return of the receipt signed by the parent. In the alternative, the court may,
               at the juvenile's first appearance or during any subsequent proceeding in the case,
               verbally advise the juvenile's parent in-person that the parent is being joined as
               a respondent to the case involving the juvenile, and order the parent to appear at
               each court appearance scheduled thereafter. Service by advisement is complete when
               the parent is advised on the record of the joinder.
(2)
Failure to appear - contempt.
Should a parent who has been properly joined in a juvenile case fail to appear as
               ordered by the court, the judge shall have the power to issue a citation to the parent
               for the failure to appear. The citation shall command the parent to appear before
               the municipal court to show cause why the parent should not be punished for contempt.
               Upon appearance of the parent on such show cause order, if the court finds that the
               failure to appear was not justified by good cause or excusable neglect, the court
               may impose punitive sanctions under its contempt powers under subsection (m) of this
               section. For purposes of this chapter, "parent" means a natural or adoptive parent,
               and includes the juvenile's guardian, legal custodian, or the person with whom the
               juvenile resides, if other than the juvenile's parent, guardian, or legal custodian.
(3)
Emancipated minor.
This subsection (h) shall not apply to any person whose parental rights have been
               terminated pursuant to the provisions of the Colorado Children's Code or the parent
               of an emancipated minor. If the parent of a juvenile cannot be found, the court may,
               in its discretion, proceed with the case without the presence of a parent.
(i)
Sentencing authority.
(1)
Sentencing options.
A municipal court judge may sentence a defendant to pay a fine or to be imprisoned
               as set forth in
section 1-5
of this Code. As part of any sentence, a judge may impose any reasonable condition
               deemed appropriate by the judge based on all facts and circumstances known to the
               judge. These conditions include, but are not limited to, ordering a defendant to:
(i)
Undergo a mental health, substance abuse, or other evaluation as the judge may deem
               appropriate to the facts of the case, and to complete any treatment or classes recommended
               as a result of the evaluation;
(ii)
Complete a class or other educational endeavor;
(iii)
Perform useful public service or community service work at a non-profit or other entity
               deemed appropriate by the judge. In the case of a juvenile, the judge may order the
               juvenile to perform useful public service or community service work at a non-profit
               or other entity deemed appropriate by the judge, or to perform community service for
               the juvenile's parent, but only if performing such service for the juvenile's parent
               would be in the best interests of the juvenile. For purposes of this chapter, "juvenile"
               means a municipal court defendant who is under the age of 18 years on the date of
               the violation;
(iv)
Utilize or participate in existing community resources, including, but not limited
               to: veterans' services, services for those experiencing homelessness, or services
               for the under- or unemployed. In ordering a defendant to utilize an existing community
               resource, a judge may specify the nature of the service and may designate a specific
               service provider, as deemed appropriate to the facts of the case;
(v)
Have no contact with a victim, witness, or co-defendant in the case;
(vi)
Not return to the location of the offense;
(vii)
Pay restitution to a victim in an amount ordered by the judge, except that restitution
               shall not be ordered in a misdemeanor traffic offense or noncriminal traffic infraction
               case. Restitution shall be ordered according to the following procedure and any other
               procedures promulgated by the presiding municipal court judge:
(A)
The city attorney must determine and submit to the court and the defendant the specific
               amount of restitution within 60 days immediately following the court's sentencing
               order or order of a deferred judgment or sentence, unless good cause is shown for
               extending the time period prior to the expiration of the 60-day period.
(B)
If the defendant contests the amount of restitution submitted by the city attorney,
               the defendant must request the court set the matter for a restitution hearing at the
               defendant's court hearing immediately following the submission of a restitution request
               by the city attorney. If the defendant does not request the hearing at that court
               hearing, the defendant waives the right to the restitution hearing and will be deemed
               to have agreed to the restitution amount.
(C)
At a restitution hearing, the city attorney must prove the restitution amount by a
               preponderance of the evidence.
(D)
The court shall award the amount of restitution it determines has been proven by the
               city attorney and actually suffered by the victim as a result of the defendant's conduct
               in the case.
(E)
For purposes of this section, "restitution" means any pecuniary loss suffered by a
               victim and includes but is not limited to all out-of-pocket expenses, interest, loss
               of use of money, anticipated future expenses, rewards paid by victims, money advanced
               by law enforcement agencies, money advanced by a governmental agency for a service
               animal, adjustment expenses, and other losses or injuries proximately caused by a
               defendant's conduct and that can be reasonably calculated and recompensed in money.
               "Restitution" does not include damages for physical or mental pain and suffering,
               loss of consortium, loss of enjoyment of life, loss of future earnings, or punitive
               damages.
(viii)
Be evaluated by a probation officer and placed on probation for a period not to exceed
               12 months from the date of sentencing. In placing a juvenile on probation, a municipal
               court judge may, upon a finding that one or more home visits by a probation officer
               is in the juvenile's best interest, order a probation officer to conduct a home visit
               or visits at the juvenile's home or place of abode, and may order a police officer
               to accompany a probation officer on the visit or visits; and
(ix)
Perform any other action or engage in any other activity or refrain from performing
               any other action or engaging in any other activity as the judge may deem appropriate
               based on the facts of the case and within the bounds of the law.
(2)
Parental responsibility.
Whenever a parent has been properly joined in a juvenile case as set forth in subsection
               (h) of this section, and a plea or finding of guilty is entered, a judge may order
               the parent to:
(i)
Cooperate in a pre-sentence investigation as directed by the court;
(ii)
Attend classes or counseling sessions designed to contribute to the rehabilitation
               of the juvenile or the parent's ability to provide proper parental care and supervision
               of the juvenile;
(iii)
Complete useful public service or community service designed to contribute to the
               rehabilitation of the juvenile;
(iv)
Make restitution to the victim as otherwise set forth in this section; and
(v)
Pay any court costs, fees, or fines imposed in the matter.
In a case where a parent fails to comply with the order of a judge under this subsection,
               the judge shall have power to issue a contempt citation to the parent for the failure
               to comply. The citation shall command the parent to appear before the municipal court
               to show cause why the parent should not be punished for contempt. Upon appearance
               of the parent on such show cause order, if the court finds that the failure to comply
               was not justified by good cause or excusable neglect, the court may impose punitive
               sanctions under its contempt powers under subsection (m) of this section.
(3)
Proof of completion.
A municipal court judge may require a defendant, parent, or other person subject
               to an order of the court to show proof of completion of a sentence, condition, requirement,
               or other order of the court.
(4)
Stay or suspension of sentence.
A municipal court judge may stay or suspend all or a portion of a sentence, including,
               but not limited to, a fine, imprisonment, community service work, or any other sentencing
               condition imposed in a case on condition of successful completion of any component
               of a sentence ordered by a judge.
(j)
Probation.
A probation officer shall report directly to the municipal court administrator. A
               probation officer has all the powers and duties set forth in C.R.S. § 19-2.5-1107,
               as may be from time to time amended, except those which by their nature cannot apply
               to municipal proceedings. A probation officer shall conduct investigations of, evaluate,
               and supervise probationers in conformance with the probation officer's job description
               and as otherwise set forth herein.
(k)
Appeals.
Appeals from the municipal court shall be in accordance with C.R.S. §§ 13-6-310 and
               16-2-114, and the applicable rules of procedure set forth in C.R.S. § 13-10-116, as
               these statutes may be from time to time amended.
(l)
Bail.
A municipal court judge may by rule designate the court administrator, the deputy
               court administrator, a court clerk, or any responsible and appropriate member of the
               Arvada police department to admit a person arrested and in the custody of the police
               department to bail. The presiding municipal court judge shall provide by rule for
               the conditions and circumstances under which such admission to bail will be granted
               pending appearance before the court and the amount of bail to be required for various
               types of violation. The bail so required may, at the election of the accused, be in
               the form of cash security, real property, tangible or intangible personal property,
               or an acceptable corporate surety bond, or a bond with adequate or acceptable private
               sureties. When provided by rule promulgated by the presiding municipal court judge,
               bail may be upon personal recognizance without security or surety. Except as otherwise
               set forth herein, the giving of bail shall be in accordance with Rule 246 of the Municipal
               Court Rules of Procedure promulgated by the Colorado Supreme Court.
(m)
Contempt - presumption and penalties.
(1)
Presumption of a willful act.
For purposes of a contempt proceeding under subsection
58-1
(f) or (g), proof that the summons or subpoena was duly served or that the person
               was otherwise properly advised of the obligation to appear, that the person was not
               excused from appearance by the court, and that the person failed to appear at the
               time scheduled shall raise a rebuttable presumption that the failure to appear was
               willful.
(2)
Adult.
Any person 18 years of age or older who is found by a municipal court judge to be
               in contempt under subsections
58-1
(e), (f), (g), or (h) shall, for each offense, be subject to a penalty not to exceed
               six months in jail or a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, or both such fine and imprisonment.
(3)
Juvenile.
Any juvenile who is found by a municipal court judge to be in contempt under subsections
58-1
(e), (f), or (g) shall, for each offense, be subject to a penalty not to exceed $1,000.00
               or performing useful public service or community service work in accordance with the
               provision of this section, or both such fine and service.
(i)
In addition, a juvenile may be sentenced to in-home detention for a period not to
               exceed 90 days. As part of an in-home detention penalty, a municipal court judge may
               issue a specific order or orders that allow for or restrict the juvenile's ability
               to engage in certain activities or attend certain events during the period of in-home
               detention.
(4)
Stay or suspension of penalty.
A municipal court judge may stay or suspend all or a portion of a penalty for contempt,
               including, but not limited to, a fine, imprisonment, useful public service or community
               service work, in-home detention, or any other penalty imposed in a case on condition
               that the contemptuous behavior not be repeated, or upon successful completion of any
               component of a sentence or penalty ordered by a judge.
(n)
Defense counsel.
(1)
Appointment.
A municipal court judge may appoint counsel at the city's expense for a defendant
               deemed indigent when:
(i)
The defendant is an adult charged with a municipal ordinance violation or misdemeanor
               traffic offense where imprisonment is a possibility and for which the city attorney
               is recommending imprisonment; or
(ii)
The defendant is an adult about whom a motion to impose a suspended jail sentence
               has been filed.
(2)
Determination of indigency.
A municipal court judge must, following diligent inquiry, make a finding on the record
               that a defendant is indigent before appointing counsel for the defendant.
(3)
Serves under contract.
An attorney appointed to serve as counsel for a municipal court defendant under this
               subsection shall work under a contract with the city.
(
Ord. No. 4830
, § 1, 12-5-2022; Ord. No.
4849
, § 1, 7-10-2023)
